items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: Tony’s got a lot of that in him.

ctx.x: All right. I like Antonio Hart. He reminds me of Cannonball some, who was my absolute hero.

He’s a talented guy. This guy has so much talent, man, he’s got to find some way — you know, hold him. He’s brilliant man. He knows so much. He loves music so much that he just, you know, it’s probably hard for him to relate to too much outside of music. And it’s been wonderful working with him because he’s a very serious — whatever he plays he’s very serious about it. He plays a lot of different styles you know. But see when I was in Berlin I worked with Leo Wright. Leo Wright and Carmell Jones. We were in one…

them all with conviction. It was one of the most fantastic things I ever saw. He could play country-western, he could play the blues, he could play old style, he could play traditional, he could play straight ahead, he could play like Trane. It was unbelievable. And the guys were actually mad at him because the guy could play so many styles they hired him for everything. He could read everything in sight. Tony’s got a lot of that in him.
